The YoY growth was driven by a sales increase of 13% YoY, a 40bps YoY fatter GM, and bigger profits among subsidiaries (Bt57m, up 161% YoY ). Including a Bt17m gain for its insurance b iz’s investment portfolio (versus an Bt18m loss in 1Q25 ), COM7 marked a 1Q26 net profit of Bt1,226m, up by 25% YoY and 2% QoQ and the second straight quarter of a new record high. Result highlights 1Q26 sales totaled Bt23.5bn, up 13% YoY but down 11% QoQ (seasonality). The YoY sales growth was driven by two factors. First, retail sales (96% of the total), rose by 11% YoY, led by smartphone sales and initial EV sales recognition. Second, receipts at adjacent businesses jumped by 67% YoY, led by a more than doubling of new loan bookings at uFund, a bigger customer base at iCare, and higher TaxiEV rental income. GM was 14.1%, up from 13.7% in 1Q25 and 12.9% in 4Q25 , boosted by increased income among adjacent businesses, which typically carry fatter margins. The receipts of adjacent businesses comprised 4.0% of COM7’s 1Q26 top-line, up from 2.7% in both 1Q25 and 4Q25. The SG&A /sales ratio was 8.3%, up from 8.0% in 1Q25, as a more conservative ECL calculation had been adopted since 4Q25. ECL was marked at Bt98m, up from Bt26m in 1Q25, while the NPL s/loans ratio remained low at below 1%. Outlook 2Q26 earnings will rise YoY, we anticipate, driven by two factors. First, IT product sales remain solid, with April sales up by 7-9% YoY, while EV deliveries should add incremental revenue. Second, income among adjacent b usinesses ( uFund, iCare, and TaxiEV) should comprise a bigger proportion of COM7’s top-line. We expect core earnings to fall QoQ on seasonality for smartphone sales. What has changed? 1Q26 core profit comprises 28% of our 2026 forecast, slightly above the three-year average first -quarter’s proportion of full-year earnings of 26%. Hence, our 2026 projection stands unchanged. Recommendation We maintain a BUY call to a target price of Bt30.
